scope.interaction: open the server-declared model-options menu, change effort, change thinking, reopen selected state, and dismiss outside

fixture.providerCapabilitySource: Existing test-only provider fixture hook enabled by T3_LYNXTRON_VIEWPORT_PROBE=1

productLoss: The Lynx model-options control cycled only the first server descriptor immediately on tap and rendered no menu.
Thinking, context window, and additional future provider descriptors were inaccessible even though the shared trigger label exposed their current values.
The fix projects every server-declared select and boolean descriptor in client-runtime, renders a dismissible menu in Lynx, and updates one descriptor while preserving the complete selection set.
harnessMismatch: The machine provider probe did not consistently expose optionDescriptors, so the final verifier uses the existing test-only provider fixture hook to supply deterministic server-declared capabilities without changing production behavior.
classification.evidenceBoundary: This exact-bundle run closes Native content, Effort and Thinking interaction, persistence, selected reopen state, dismissal, and runtime. It does not claim menu pixel parity or physical keyboard interaction.

menu.text: Reasoning High Extra High Context window 200k 1M Thinking On Off

effortMutation.input: DevTool Input.emulateTouchFromMouseEvent on measured model-option trigger and unselected effort row

thinkingMutation.input: DevTool Input.emulateTouchFromMouseEvent on the measured Thinking On row

typecheck.clientRuntime: pass with one pre-existing Effect suggestion

build.native: pass with existing unsupported-property and import.meta warnings

validation.agentBrowserLeakGate: Every owned loop reported owned=0 orphaned=0; external sessions were informational only.

remainingRisk: Menu geometry, typography, and material are not compared against Web in this behavior slice.
Keyboard navigation and Escape dismissal remain pending a physical keyboard or authorized Computer Use session.
Provider prompt-injected options such as Ultrathink remain governed by Web prompt semantics and are not exercised by this Native fixture.
